45.title: Lost update: where did +10 go? Oracle isolation levels explained 🔒 #sql #oracle #shorts
45.yt:
45. Balance 100. Cashier A adds 10, cashier B adds 50.
Final balance: 150 😱 Where did +10 go?

🔍 READ COMMITTED (default) is per STATEMENT
   → each query sees data committed before it began
   → readers never block writers · dirty reads impossible
🔁 Same SELECT twice in one transaction → can differ
💥 Lost update: read → compute in the app → write back
   → last write wins, no error
✅ 3 fixes
   → SET balance = balance + 10
   → SELECT … FOR UPDATE
   → version column: 0 rows updated → retry
🧊 SERIALIZABLE: one snapshot for the whole transaction
   → ORA-08177 can't serialize access → retry
📊 SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY for consistent reports
🚫 No READ UNCOMMITTED in Oracle

Never read, compute, write without a lock 💡

46.title: SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED: build a safe job queue 🔐 #sql #oracle #shorts
46.yt:
46. 5 workers. 1 queue. The same job paid 5 times 💸
Or everyone waits all night ⏳

🔒 FOR UPDATE locks the selected rows until COMMIT / ROLLBACK
   → plain SELECTs still read them
⏱️ How long to wait?
   → default: forever
   → NOWAIT → ORA-00054 resource busy
   → WAIT 3 → ORA-30006 after 3 seconds
🚀 SKIP LOCKED: rows locked by others are skipped
   → every worker gets its own jobs, nobody waits
🧑‍💻 Cursor … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + BULK COLLECT LIMIT 10
⚠️ ROWNUM 10 + SKIP LOCKED can return 0 rows
   → ROWNUM picks rows BEFORE locked ones are skipped
🎯 FOR UPDATE OF j.status · WHERE CURRENT OF c
🚫 COMMIT inside a FOR UPDATE loop → ORA-01002

Lock what you process, skip what others hold 💡

Do you use SKIP LOCKED for queues? 👇

47.title: DATE traps in Oracle: why your report misses the last day 📅 #sql #oracle #shorts
47.yt:
47. WHERE created BETWEEN DATE '2026-11-01' AND DATE '2026-11-30'
Nov 30 payments: missing 😱

🕛 An Oracle DATE always has a time
   → DATE '2026-11-30' = midnight
✅ Half-open range
   → from Nov 1 inclusive, up to Dec 1 exclusive
   → index friendly, no TRUNC on the column
⏱️ TIMESTAMP: fractions up to 9 digits (default 6)
➗ DATE − DATE = days (0.5 = 12 h)
   TS − TS = INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND
🌍 SYSDATE = DB server clock · CURRENT_DATE = session time zone
   → TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE for global apps
📆 ADD_MONTHS(Jan 31, 1) → Feb 28
   → + INTERVAL '1' MONTH → ORA-01839
🚫 TO_DATE without a format depends on NLS settings

A date has a time. Use half-open ranges 💡

48.title: Hierarchical queries: a whole tree in one SELECT 🌳 #sql #oracle #shorts
48.yt:
48. Org chart. Chart of accounts. Bill of materials 🌳
Every row points to its parent. One SELECT for the whole tree?

🧬 Table: id, parent_id, name
🔗 START WITH parent_id IS NULL
   CONNECT BY PRIOR id = parent_id
   → LEVEL = depth, indent with LPAD
🧰 SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH · CONNECT_BY_ISLEAF
   CONNECT_BY_ROOT · ORDER SIBLINGS BY
🔄 Loop in data → ORA-01436
   → NOCYCLE + CONNECT_BY_ISCYCLE
⚠️ WHERE filters rows, children stay
   → condition in CONNECT BY prunes the branch
✨ 11gR2+: recursive WITH
   → SEARCH DEPTH FIRST · CYCLE clause
⚡ Index parent_id

Start with the roots, connect by prior 💡

CONNECT BY or recursive WITH: which do you use? 👇

49.title: Foreign key without an index: one DELETE locks the whole table 🔑 #sql #oracle #shorts
49.yt:
49. DELETE FROM clients WHERE id = 42
→ PAYMENTS locked, 50 sessions waiting 😱

📏 PK · UNIQUE · FK · CHECK · NOT NULL
   → ORA-00001 · 02291 · 02292 · 02290 · 01400
🔑 PK / UNIQUE create (or reuse) an index
   → FOREIGN KEY creates NONE
🔒 Unindexed FK + parent DELETE / key UPDATE
   → child table lock for the statement + full scan
   → blocking and deadlocks
✅ CREATE INDEX on the FK columns
⏳ DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED → checked at COMMIT
   → invalid? ORA-02091, whole transaction rolled back
🗄️ ENABLE NOVALIDATE: check new rows, trust old ones
⚡ Constraints help the optimizer
   → join elimination · COUNT(*) via index

Index every foreign key you delete through 💡

50.title: PIVOT & UNPIVOT in Oracle: rows into columns in one statement 🔄 #sql #oracle #shorts
50.yt:
50. Sales: one row per branch and month.
Report: one row per branch, months as columns 📊

🧮 Old way: SUM(CASE WHEN month = 'JAN' THEN amount END)
✨ 11g+: PIVOT (SUM(amount) FOR month IN ('JAN' AS jan, …))
⚠️ Hidden GROUP BY: every other column groups
   → an id column = one row per id
   → always pivot from an inline view
➕ Several aggregates → JAN_TOTAL, JAN_CNT…
📌 IN list = constants only
   → dynamic SQL or PIVOT XML … ANY
🔄 UNPIVOT: columns back to rows
   → NULLs dropped unless INCLUDE NULLS
⚡ Same speed as CASE: one pass, one GROUP BY

Pivot from an inline view, filter before you pivot 💡

PIVOT or CASE: what's in your reports? 👇
